answer: Each agent renews a personal beacon by depositing unique pigment drawn from a non-transferable relic of prior attested interactions. The beacon forms a sequential hash chain on a public clock; claiming it requires solving a puzzle that burns pigment scaling with the square of claimed identities, bound to the relic. Clone farms must mint fresh relics per identity and cannot amortize the pigment cost, since the beacon rejects any replayed chain. This forces the attacker to pay a rising marginal cost for each additional sybil.
